qualification.reason: This document is a solicitation issued by the City of Providence for parking signs and related materials, containing a request for proposals, scope of work, submission instructions, deadlines, and evaluation criteria.

quotes.quote: REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS
Item Description:  PARKING SIGNS, PARKING SIGN POSTS, AND RELATED PARKING ADMINISTRATION MATERIALS – ONE-YEAR CONTRACT WITH TWO ONE-YEAR RENEWAL OPTIONS
Date to be opened: 7/27/2026
CITY OF PROVIDENCE INVITATION FOR BIDS (IFB)

1. Purpose The City of Providence Department of Public Works, Parking Administration Division, seeks competitive bids from qualified manufacturers and distributors for the furnishing and delivery of parking regulatory signs, parking sign posts, mounting hardware, parking control devices, and related materials on an as-needed basis under a firm fixed unit price requirements contract.
Bids may be submitted up to 2:15 P.M. on the above meeting date at the Department of the City Clerk.

findings.title: Conflicting Statements on Installation Services Inclusion
findings.fact: Section 7 states 'At the City's option, the Contractor may also provide sign installation services as described in Section 7A (Optional Add/Alternate Sign Installation Services). Installation services shall not be included in the base bid and shall only be performed when specifically authorized by the City through a purchase order or work authorization.' However, Section 8 is titled 'Optional Add/Alternate Sign Installation Services' and describes installation services in detail, but the numbering is inconsistent (Section 7A vs Section 8).
findings.business_implication: The inconsistency may cause confusion about whether installation services are part of the base bid or optional.
findings.action_recommendation: Clarify with the City whether installation services are optional and how they will be evaluated.

quotes.quote: At the City's option, the Contractor may also provide sign installation services as described in Section 7A (Optional Add/Alternate Sign Installation Services). Installation services shall not be included in the base bid and shall only be performed when specifically authorized by the City through a purchase order or work authorization.
8. Optional Add/Alternate Sign Installation Services

findings.title: Broad Indemnification
findings.fact: The contractor shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the City from any and all claims, damages, losses, etc., arising out of the performance of the work.
findings.business_implication: Bidder assumes significant liability for claims and legal costs, potentially beyond typical limits.
findings.action_recommendation: Review insurance coverage and consider the extent of indemnification obligations.

quotes.quote: To the fullest extent permitted by law, you shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the City, its employees, officers, agents, and assigns from and against any and all claims, damages, losses, allegations, demands, actions, causes of action, suits, obligations, fines, penalties, judgments, liabilities, costs and expenses, including but not limited to attorneys’ fees, of any nature whatsoever arising out of, in connection with, or resulting from the performance of the work provided in the Agreement.

findings.title: No Limitation of Liability
findings.fact: The City does not agree to limit the contractor's liability to the price of the Agreement or any other monetary limit.
findings.business_implication: Bidder faces unlimited liability for claims arising from the contract.
findings.action_recommendation: Assess risk exposure and consider whether to seek clarification or negotiate liability caps.

quotes.quote: The City shall have the time permitted within the applicable statute of limitations, and no less, to bring or assert any and all causes of action, suits, claims or demands the City may have arising out of, in connection with, or resulting from the performance of the work provided in the Agreement, and in no event does the City agree to limit your liability to the price of the Agreement or any other monetary limit.

findings.title: Conflicting Information on Installation Services
findings.fact: Section 7 states installation services shall not be included in the base bid and shall only be performed when specifically authorized. Section 8 states the City may award installation to the same contractor or not at all. However, Section 23 states the City reserves the right to award installation to a different contractor through a separate procurement.
findings.business_implication: There is ambiguity regarding whether installation can be awarded to a different contractor.
findings.action_recommendation: Clarify with the City whether installation may be awarded separately.

quotes.quote: At the City's option, the Contractor may also provide sign installation services as described in Section 7A (Optional Add/Alternate Sign Installation Services). Installation services shall not be included in the base bid and shall only be performed when specifically authorized by the City through a purchase order or work authorization.

Optional Installation Services: The City reserves the right to award the optional installation services to the same contractor, to a different contractor through a separate procurement, or not to award the installation portion at all, if determined to be in the City's best interest.

findings.title: No Limitation of Liability
findings.fact: The City does not agree to limit the contractor's liability to the contract price or any other monetary limit.
findings.business_implication: The bidder faces unlimited liability for claims arising from the work, which is a significant financial risk.
findings.action_recommendation: Assess risk exposure and consider whether to seek clarification or negotiate a liability cap.

quotes.quote: The City shall not subject itself to any contractual limitations on liability.
in no event does the City agree to limit your liability to the price of the Agreement or any other monetary limit.

findings.title: Potential Conflict: MBE/WBE Certification Timing
findings.fact: Page 17 states that MBE/WBE subcontractors must be certified at the time of bid, but page 20 states that proof of certain items (including Business Tax ID) is only requested after award. This is not a direct contradiction but may create confusion about when certifications are needed.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must ensure MBE/WBE certifications are in place at bid submission, while other documents can be provided later.
findings.action_recommendation: Clarify with the City if there is any flexibility on MBE/WBE certification timing.

quotes.quote: Please note that all MBE/WBE subcontractors/suppliers must be certified by the Office of Diversity, Equity and Opportunity at the time of bid.
This information is NOT requested to be provided in your initial bid that you will submit to the City Clerk’s office by the “date to be opened” noted on page 1.

findings.title: Uncapped Indemnification and No Limitation of Liability
findings.fact: The Contractor must indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the City from any and all claims, damages, losses, etc., arising out of the work, and the City does not agree to limit the Contractor's liability to the contract price or any other monetary limit.
findings.business_implication: The bidder faces potentially unlimited financial exposure for any claims arising from the contract, including those caused by the City's own negligence, with no cap on liability.
findings.action_recommendation: Seek clarification on the scope of indemnification and request a mutual liability cap or carve-outs for consequential damages during the clarification period.

quotes.quote: To the fullest extent permitted by law, you shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the City, its employees, officers, agents, and assigns from and against any and all claims, damages, losses, allegations, demands, actions, causes of action, suits, obligations, fines, penalties, judgments, liabilities, costs and expenses, including but not limited to attorneys’ fees, of any nature whatsoever arising out of, in connection with, or resulting from the performance of the work provided in the Agreement.

The City shall not subject itself to any contractual limitations on liability. The City shall have the time permitted within the applicable statute of limitations, and no less, to bring or assert any and all causes of action, suits, claims or demands the City may have arising out of, in connection with, or resulting from the performance of the work provided in the Agreement, and in no event does the City agree to limit your liability to the price of the Agreement or any other monetary limit.

findings.title: Five Years Experience and Three Municipal References Required
findings.fact: Bidder shall have at least five years of experience manufacturing traffic control signs and provide three municipal references demonstrating comparable work.
findings.business_implication: Bidders without the required experience and references will be disqualified.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure your company meets the experience requirement and prepare three municipal references.

quotes.quote: Bidder shall have at least five years of experience manufacturing traffic control signs and provide three municipal references demonstrating comparable work.

findings.title: Deadline for Questions

findings.action_recommendation: Submit any questions before July 20, 2026.

findings.title: Award to Lowest Qualified and Responsible Bidder
findings.fact: The Board of Contract and Supply will make the award to the lowest qualified and responsible bidder.
findings.business_implication: Price is the primary factor, but bidders must also be deemed qualified and responsible.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure your bid is competitive and that you meet all qualification requirements.

quotes.quote: The Board of Contract and Supply will make the award to the lowest qualified and responsible bidder.

findings.title: Firm Fixed Unit Price Contract
findings.fact: The Contractor shall provide all awarded items at the fixed unit prices submitted in its bid for the duration of the initial contract term. Unit prices shall include all labor, materials, manufacturing, packaging, freight, delivery, overhead, profit, and all other costs necessary to furnish the requested items. Except as otherwise provided for approved renewal-term price adjustments, unit prices shall remain firm throughout the contract term.
findings.business_implication: Prices cannot be increased during the initial term, so accurate cost estimation is critical.
findings.action_recommendation: Carefully calculate all costs to ensure the fixed prices are sustainable.

quotes.quote: The Contractor shall provide all awarded items at the fixed unit prices submitted in its bid for the duration of the initial contract term. Unit prices shall include all labor, materials, manufacturing, packaging, freight, delivery, overhead, profit, and all other costs necessary to furnish the requested items. Except as otherwise provided for approved renewal-term price adjustments, unit prices shall remain firm throughout the contract term.

findings.title: No Guaranteed Minimum Purchase
findings.fact: The City does not guarantee any minimum purchase quantity.
findings.business_implication: The contractor may receive no orders or very few orders, so revenue is uncertain.
findings.action_recommendation: Consider the risk of low volume when pricing and preparing capacity.

quotes.quote: The City does not guarantee any minimum purchase quantity.

findings.title: Renewal Price Adjustment Limited to CPI-U or 3%
findings.fact: Renewal price adjustments may be requested only during renewal periods and shall not exceed the lesser of the annual CPI-U increase or three percent, supported by documentation.
findings.business_implication: Price increases are capped at 3% or CPI, whichever is lower, so cost increases may not be fully covered.
findings.action_recommendation: Factor this limitation into long-term pricing strategy.

quotes.quote: Renewal price adjustments may be requested only during renewal periods and shall not exceed the lesser of the annual CPI-U increase or three percent, supported by documentation.

findings.title: Warranty of Installation Workmanship for One Year
findings.fact: The Contractor shall warrant installation workmanship for a minimum period of one (1) year from the date of acceptance.
findings.business_implication: The contractor is responsible for defects in installation for one year after acceptance.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure quality installation and be prepared to address any warranty claims.

quotes.quote: The Contractor shall warrant installation workmanship for a minimum period of one (1) year from the date of acceptance.

findings.title: Emergency Order Priority
findings.fact: During declared emergencies, the Contractor shall prioritize City orders.
findings.business_implication: The contractor must be able to respond quickly and prioritize City orders during emergencies, which may disrupt normal operations.
findings.action_recommendation: Develop an emergency response plan and ensure capacity to handle urgent orders.

quotes.quote: During declared emergencies, the Contractor shall prioritize City orders.

findings.title: Artwork Developed for City Becomes City Property
findings.fact: Artwork developed specifically for the City shall become the property of the City.
findings.business_implication: Any custom designs created for the City will be owned by the City, limiting reuse.
findings.action_recommendation: Be aware that custom artwork will be transferred to the City.

quotes.quote: Artwork developed specifically for the City shall become the property of the City.

findings.title: Insurance Requirements Not Specified
findings.fact: A certificate of insurance will normally be required of a successful vendor.
findings.business_implication: The specific types and amounts of insurance are not detailed in the RFP.
findings.action_recommendation: Contact the purchasing department to obtain the insurance requirements before bidding.

quotes.quote: A certificate of insurance will normally be required of a successful vendor.

findings.title: Prevailing Wage Requirements Not Specified
findings.fact: For many contracts involving construction, alteration and/or repair work, State law provisions concerning payment of prevailing wage rates apply (RIGL Sec. 37-13-1 et seq.)
findings.business_implication: If installation services are awarded, prevailing wage rates may apply, increasing labor costs.
findings.action_recommendation: Determine if the installation work falls under prevailing wage requirements and factor into pricing.

quotes.quote: For many contracts involving construction, alteration and/or repair work, State law provisions concerning payment of prevailing wage rates apply (RIGL Sec. 37-13-1 et seq.)

findings.title: Financial Assurance Requirements
findings.fact: The bid terms specify that financial assurances may be required, and if the first two checkboxes are checked, the specified assurance must accompany a bid or the bid will not be considered. The third checkbox indicates the lowest responsible bidder will be contacted and required to post a bond to be awarded the contract.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must determine which financial assurance applies to this solicitation and ensure it is included with the bid to avoid disqualification.
findings.action_recommendation: Review the solicitation documents to identify which checkbox is marked and prepare the required certified check, bid bond, or performance and payment bond accordingly.

quotes.quote: Financial assurances may be required in order to be a successful bidder for Commodity or Construction and Service contracts. If either of the first two checkboxes below is checked, the specified assurance must accompany a bid, or the bid will not be considered by the Board of Contract and Supply. The third checkbox indicates the lowest responsible bidder will be contacted and required to post a bond to be awarded the contract.

findings.title: Bid Bond Requirements
findings.fact: If a bid bond is required, it must be deposited with the City Clerk, and any person signing as attorney-in-fact must include a power of attorney.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must ensure the bid bond is properly executed and includes the power of attorney if applicable, to avoid rejection.
findings.action_recommendation: If a bid bond is required, verify that the bond is in the correct amount and that any attorney-in-fact includes the power of attorney document.

quotes.quote: A bid bond in the amount of       per centum (%) of the proposed total price, must be deposited with the City Clerk as a guarantee that the contract will be signed and delivered by the bidder; and the amount of such bid bond shall be retained for the use of the City as liquidated damages in case of default. Any person signing a bid bond as an attorney-in-fact shall include with the bid bond an original, or a photocopy or facsimile of an original, power of attorney.

findings.title: Performance and Payment Bond
findings.fact: If the third checkbox is checked, the lowest responsible bidder will be required to post a performance and payment bond equal to 100% of the awarded contract.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must be prepared to obtain a performance and payment bond if awarded the contract, which may affect bonding capacity and cost.
findings.action_recommendation: Assess bonding capacity and include the cost of the bond in the bid pricing if applicable.

quotes.quote: A performance and payment bond with a satisfactory surety company will be posted by the bidder in a sum equal to one hundred per centum (100%) of the awarded contract.

findings.title: Bid Form Completion Requirements
findings.fact: Bids must be in ink or typewritten, all blanks completed, prices stated in both writing and figures, and bids must be signed in ink.
findings.business_implication: Failure to comply with these formalities may lead to rejection of the bid.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure the bid form is fully completed, prices are stated in both writing and figures, and the bid is signed in ink.

quotes.quote: Bidder’s responses must be in ink or typewritten, and all blanks on the bid form should be completed.
The price or prices proposed should be stated both in WRITING and in FIGURES, and any proposal not so stated may be rejected.
All bids MUST BE SIGNED IN INK.

findings.title: Local Agent for Service of Process
findings.fact: If the bidder is based outside Rhode Island, they must list a local agent for service of process located within Rhode Island.
findings.business_implication: Out-of-state bidders must have a Rhode Island agent for service of process, which may require additional arrangements.
findings.action_recommendation: If bidding from out of state, identify and list a local agent for service of process on the bid form.

quotes.quote: If the bidder’s company is based in a state other than Rhode Island, list name and contact information for a local agent for service of process that is located within Rhode Island

findings.title: Certification of Bidder (Non-Discrimination/Hiring)
findings.fact: The bidder must certify that it does not unlawfully discriminate and that all employees have been hired in compliance with applicable laws.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must be able to make this certification truthfully; false certification could have legal consequences.
findings.action_recommendation: Review hiring practices to ensure compliance and have an authorized representative sign the certification.

quotes.quote: Bidder does not unlawfully discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation and/or religion in its business and hiring practices.
All of Bidder’s employees have been hired in compliance with all applicable federal, state and local laws, rules and regulations.

findings.title: Public Records Certification
findings.fact: All bids become public record upon receipt and opening, and bidders must not submit sensitive information directly to the issuing department to protect pricing; doing so will result in disqualification.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must be aware that all submitted information will be public and must not attempt to submit information separately to protect pricing.
findings.action_recommendation: Do not submit any part of the bid directly to the issuing department; include all required information in the bid packet submitted to the City Clerk.

quotes.quote: All bids submitted in response to Requests for Proposals (RFP’s) and Requests for Qualification (RFQ’s), documents contained within, and the details outlined on those documents become public record upon receipt by the City Clerk’s office and opening at the corresponding Board of Contract and Supply (BOCS) meeting.

The City of Providence observes a public and transparent bidding process. Information required in the bidding packet may not be submitted directly to the issuing department at the discretion of the bidder in order to protect other information, such as pricing terms, from becoming public. Bidders who make such an attempt will be disqualified.

findings.title: Affidavit of City Vendor
findings.fact: The bidder must complete an affidavit disclosing campaign contributions to certain city officials and candidates within the past 12 months.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must gather information on any campaign contributions made by the business, its owners, executive officers, and their spouses/dependents to Providence city officials.
findings.action_recommendation: Complete the affidavit accurately, listing all required individuals and any contributions made.

quotes.quote: Within the 12 month period preceding the date of this bid submission with the City of Providence, or with respect to the contracts that are not in writing within the 12 month period preceding the date of notification that the contract has reached the $100,000 threshold, have you made campaign contributions within a calendar year to (please list all persons or entities required under Sec. 21.-28.1 (e)).

findings.title: Award and Price Firmness
findings.fact: Awards will be made within 90 days of bid opening, and all bid prices will be considered firm unless qualified otherwise; requests for price increases will not be honored.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must be prepared to hold its pricing for at least 90 days and cannot request price increases during that period.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure pricing is valid for at least 90 days and avoid any qualifications that might be rejected.

quotes.quote: Awards will be made within nighty (90) days of bid opening. All bid prices will be considered firm, unless qualified otherwise. Requests for price increases will not be honored.

findings.title: Payment for Partial Delivery (Commodity)
findings.fact: For commodity bids, payment for partial delivery will not be allowed except when provided for in blanket or term contracts.
findings.business_implication: The bidder may not receive payment for partial deliveries unless the contract is a blanket or term contract.
findings.action_recommendation: If bidding on a commodity contract, understand the payment terms and structure deliveries accordingly.

quotes.quote: Payment for partial delivery will not be allowed except when provided for in blanket or term contracts.

findings.title: Shipping Charge for Partial Deliveries (Construction/Service)
findings.fact: For construction and service contracts, only one shipping charge will be applied in the event of partial deliveries for blanket or term contracts.

findings.action_recommendation: If bidding on a construction or service contract, ensure shipping charges are structured to comply with this term.

quotes.quote: Only one shipping charge will be applied in the event of partial deliveries for blanket or term contracts.

findings.title: Workers' Compensation Compliance
findings.fact: Prior to commencing performance, the successful bidder must attest to compliance with the Rhode Island Worker’s Compensation Act, or submit a sworn affidavit if exempt.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must ensure it is in compliance with workers' compensation laws or be prepared to provide an exemption affidavit.

quotes.quote: Prior to commencing performance under the contract, the successful bidder shall attest to compliance with the provisions of the Rhode Island Worker’s Compensation Act, RIGL 28-29-1, et seq.  If exempt from compliance, the successful bidder shall submit a sworn Affidavit by a corporate officer to that effect, which shall accompany the signed contract.

findings.title: Certificate of Insurance

findings.action_recommendation: Ensure insurance coverage is in place and obtain a certificate of insurance that meets the City's requirements.

quotes.quote: Prior to commencing performance under the contract, the successful bidder shall, submit a certificate of insurance, in a form and in an amount satisfactory to the City.

findings.fact: Failure to deliver within the time quoted or failure to meet specifications may result in default, but deliveries are subject to strikes, lockouts, accidents, and Acts of God.

findings.business_implication: Prices must be firm for the initial term, with limited renewal adjustments.
findings.action_recommendation: Price carefully to cover all costs.

quotes.quote: The Contractor shall provide all awarded items at the fixed unit prices submitted in its bid for the duration of the initial contract term. Unit prices shall include all labor, materials, manufacturing, packaging, freight, delivery, overhead, profit, and all other costs necessary to furnish the requested items.

findings.title: No Guaranteed Minimum Purchase
findings.fact: The City does not guarantee any minimum purchase quantity.
findings.business_implication: The contractor may receive no orders or very few orders, so revenue is uncertain.
findings.action_recommendation: Consider the risk of low volume when pricing.

quotes.quote: The City does not guarantee any minimum purchase quantity.

findings.title: Renewal Price Adjustment Limited
findings.fact: Renewal price adjustments may be requested only during renewal periods and shall not exceed the lesser of the annual CPI-U increase or three percent, supported by documentation.
findings.business_implication: Price increases are capped at 3% or CPI, whichever is lower, during renewals.
findings.action_recommendation: Factor this limitation into long-term pricing strategy.

quotes.quote: Renewal price adjustments may be requested only during renewal periods and shall not exceed the lesser of the annual CPI-U increase or three percent, supported by documentation.

findings.title: Warranty and Defective Product Replacement
findings.fact: Defective or non-conforming materials shall be replaced within five business days at no additional cost. Provide a minimum ten-year manufacturer's warranty covering reflectivity, delamination, peeling, cracking, corrosion, fading, adhesive failure, ink failure, and manufacturing defects.
findings.business_implication: The contractor bears the cost of replacing defective products and must provide a long warranty.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure product quality and warranty terms are acceptable.

quotes.quote: Defective or non-conforming materials shall be replaced within five business days at no additional cost.
Provide a minimum ten-year manufacturer's warranty covering reflectivity, delamination, peeling, cracking, corrosion, fading, adhesive failure, ink failure, and manufacturing defects.

findings.title: City's Right to Terminate or Reject Bids
findings.fact: The City reserves the right to reject any or all bids, waive minor informalities, and determine the bid most advantageous to the City.
findings.business_implication: The City has broad discretion in awarding the contract.
findings.action_recommendation: Be aware that the City may reject all bids.

quotes.quote: The City reserves the right to request clarifications, product literature, samples, and additional information prior to award, waive minor informalities, reject any or all bids, and determine the bid most advantageous to the City.

findings.title: Shareable Contract
findings.fact: At the City's discretion, other governmental, quasi-governmental, educational, and public agencies may purchase from the resulting contract under the same terms and conditions.
findings.business_implication: The contractor may be required to supply other agencies at the same prices.
findings.action_recommendation: Consider the potential volume and pricing implications.

quotes.quote: At the City's discretion, other governmental, quasi-governmental, educational, and public agencies may purchase from the resulting contract under the same terms and conditions.

findings.title: Emergency Order Priority
findings.fact: During declared emergencies, the Contractor shall prioritize City orders.
findings.business_implication: The contractor must be able to respond quickly during emergencies, potentially disrupting normal operations.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure capacity to handle emergency orders.

quotes.quote: During declared emergencies, the Contractor shall prioritize City orders.

findings.title: Out-of-State Corporation Registration Requirement
findings.fact: A bidder who is an out-of-state corporation shall qualify or register to transact business in this State, in accordance with the Rhode Island Business Corporation Act, RIGL Sec. 7-1.2-1401, et seq.
findings.business_implication: Out-of-state bidders must complete registration with the Rhode Island Secretary of State before bidding, which may take time and incur fees.
findings.action_recommendation: Verify registration status and initiate registration process early if not already registered.

quotes.quote: A bidder who is an out-of-state corporation shall qualify or register to transact business in this State, in accordance with the Rhode Island Business Corporation Act, RIGL Sec. 7-1.2-1401, et seq.

findings.title: Two Copies of Bid Required
findings.fact: Submit 2 copies of the bid to the City Clerk, unless the specification section of this document indicates otherwise.
findings.business_implication: Bidder must prepare and submit two complete copies of the bid to avoid rejection.
findings.action_recommendation: Prepare two identical bid packages and ensure both are submitted by the deadline.

quotes.quote: Submit 2 copies of the bid to the City Clerk, unless the specification section of this document indicates otherwise.

findings.title: Non-Discrimination Certification Required
findings.fact: Bidder must certify that it does not unlawfully discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation and/or religion in its business and hiring practices and that all of its employees are lawfully employed under all applicable federal, state and local laws, rules and regulations. (See Bid Form 2.)
findings.business_implication: Bidder must complete and submit Bid Form 2 as part of the bid package.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure Bid Form 2 is completed and signed by an authorized representative.

quotes.quote: Bidder must certify that it does not unlawfully discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation and/or religion in its business and hiring practices and that all of its employees are lawfully employed under all applicable federal, state and local laws, rules and regulations. (See Bid Form 2.)

findings.title: Prices Firm for 90 Days
findings.fact: Awards will be made within nighty (90) days of bid opening. All bid prices will be considered firm, unless qualified otherwise. Requests for price increases will not be honored.
findings.business_implication: Bidder must hold its quoted prices for at least 90 days and cannot increase prices during that period.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure pricing strategy accounts for potential cost increases over the 90-day period.

quotes.quote: Awards will be made within nighty (90) days of bid opening. All bid prices will be considered firm, unless qualified otherwise. Requests for price increases will not be honored.

findings.title: Unit Price Governs in Case of Error
findings.fact: In case of error in the extension of prices quoted, the unit price will govern.
findings.business_implication: Bidder must ensure unit prices are accurate, as they will be binding in case of arithmetic errors.
findings.action_recommendation: Double-check all unit prices and extensions before submission.

quotes.quote: In case of error in the extension of prices quoted, the unit price will govern.

findings.title: No Cash Discounts Considered
findings.fact: In determining the lowest responsible bidder, cash discounts based on preferable payment terms will not be considered.
findings.business_implication: Offering cash discounts will not improve the bid's competitiveness.
findings.action_recommendation: Do not rely on cash discounts to win the bid; focus on base pricing.

quotes.quote: In determining the lowest responsible bidder, cash discounts based on preferable payment terms will not be considered.

findings.title: Tax Exemption
findings.fact: As the City of Providence is exempt from the payment of Federal Excise Taxes and Rhode Island Sales Tax, prices quoted are not to include these taxes.
findings.business_implication: Bidder must exclude federal excise and Rhode Island sales taxes from quoted prices.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure pricing does not include these taxes.

quotes.quote: As the City of Providence is exempt from the payment of Federal Excise Taxes and Rhode Island Sales Tax, prices quoted are not to include these taxes.

findings.title: Delivery Dates Must Be Shown
findings.fact: Delivery dates must be shown in the bid. If no delivery date is specified, it will be assumed that an immediate delivery from stock will be made.
findings.business_implication: Bidder must specify delivery dates; otherwise, immediate delivery is assumed, which may be impossible to meet.
findings.action_recommendation: Clearly state realistic delivery dates in the bid.

quotes.quote: Delivery dates must be shown in the bid. If no delivery date is specified, it will be assumed that an immediate delivery from stock will be made.

findings.title: No Goods Without Purchase Order
findings.fact: No goods should be delivered, or work started without a Purchase Order.
findings.business_implication: Bidder must not commence work or deliver goods until a purchase order is issued.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure a purchase order is received before starting performance.

quotes.quote: No goods should be delivered, or work started without a Purchase Order.

findings.title: Performance and Payment Bond Required
findings.fact: A performance and payment bond with a satisfactory surety company will be posted by the bidder in a sum equal to one hundred per centum (100%) of the awarded contract.
findings.business_implication: If this checkbox is checked, the successful bidder must obtain a performance and payment bond for the full contract amount, which may involve additional costs.
findings.action_recommendation: Budget for bond costs and arrange for bonding capacity.

quotes.quote: A performance and payment bond with a satisfactory surety company will be posted by the bidder in a sum equal to one hundred per centum (100%) of the awarded contract.

findings.title: Certificate of Insurance Required
findings.fact: Prior to commencing performance under the contract, the successful bidder shall, submit a certificate of insurance, in a form and in an amount satisfactory to the City.
findings.business_implication: Bidder must obtain and provide a certificate of insurance before starting work.
findings.action_recommendation: Secure appropriate insurance coverage and be ready to provide the certificate.

quotes.quote: Prior to commencing performance under the contract, the successful bidder shall, submit a certificate of insurance, in a form and in an amount satisfactory to the City.

findings.title: No Assignment Without Consent
findings.fact: The contractor will NOT be permitted to: a) assign or underlet the contract, or b) assign either legally or equitably any monies or any claim thereto without the previous written consent of the City Purchasing Director.
findings.business_implication: Bidder cannot transfer the contract or payments without City approval, limiting flexibility.
findings.action_recommendation: Plan to perform the contract directly; seek consent if assignment becomes necessary.

quotes.quote: The contractor will NOT be permitted to: a) assign or underlet the contract, or b) assign either legally or equitably any monies or any claim thereto without the previous written consent of the City Purchasing Director.

findings.title: Workers' Compensation Compliance
findings.fact: Prior to commencing performance under the contract, the successful bidder shall attest to compliance with the provisions of the Rhode Island Worker’s Compensation Act, RIGL 28-29-1, et seq. If exempt from compliance, the successful bidder shall submit a sworn Affidavit by a corporate officer to that effect, which shall accompany the signed contract.
findings.business_implication: Bidder must provide proof of workers' compensation insurance or an exemption affidavit before starting work.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure workers' compensation coverage is in place or prepare the exemption affidavit.

quotes.quote: Prior to commencing performance under the contract, the successful bidder shall attest to compliance with the provisions of the Rhode Island Worker’s Compensation Act, RIGL 28-29-1, et seq. If exempt from compliance, the successful bidder shall submit a sworn Affidavit by a corporate officer to that effect, which shall accompany the signed contract.

findings.title: Bid Form Completion Requirements
findings.fact: Bids must be in ink or typewritten, all blanks completed, prices stated in writing and figures, bids totaled, and signed in ink.
findings.business_implication: Failure to comply with these formalities may lead to rejection of the bid.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure the bid form is fully completed, prices are stated both in words and figures, totals are provided, and the form is signed in ink.

quotes.quote: Bidder’s responses must be in ink or typewritten, and all blanks on the bid form should be completed.
The price or prices proposed should be stated both in WRITING and in FIGURES, and any proposal not so stated may be rejected.
Bids SHOULD BE TOTALED so that the final cost is clearly stated (unless submitting a unit price bid), however each item should be priced individually.
All bids MUST BE SIGNED IN INK.

findings.title: Local Agent for Service of Process
findings.fact: If the bidder's company is based in a state other than Rhode Island, the bidder must list name and contact information for a local agent for service of process located within Rhode Island.
findings.business_implication: Out-of-state bidders must have a local agent in Rhode Island, which may involve additional cost or administrative burden.
findings.action_recommendation: If bidding from outside Rhode Island, arrange for a local agent and provide their details on the bid form.

quotes.quote: If the bidder’s company is based in a state other than Rhode Island, list name and contact information for a local agent for service of process that is located within Rhode Island

findings.title: Annual Cost Specification for Multi-Year Contracts
findings.fact: Contracts exceeding twelve months must specify annual costs for each year.
findings.business_implication: For multi-year bids, the bidder must provide a cost breakdown per year, which may affect pricing strategy and total bid evaluation.
findings.action_recommendation: If the contract term exceeds one year, prepare annual cost figures for each year and include them in the bid.

quotes.quote: Contracts exceeding twelve months must specify annual costs for each year.

findings.title: Award Basis: Total or Individual Items
findings.fact: Awards may be made on the basis of total bid or by individual items.
findings.business_implication: The bidder cannot assume the award will be based on the total bid; the buyer may select individual items, affecting pricing strategy.
findings.action_recommendation: Price each item competitively and be prepared for partial awards.

quotes.quote: Awards may be made on the basis of total bid or by individual items.

findings.title: Public Record Disclosure of Bids
findings.fact: All bids submitted in response to RFPs/RFQs, documents contained within, and the details outlined on those documents become public record upon receipt by the City Clerk's office and opening at the corresponding Board of Contract and Supply (BOCS) meeting.
findings.business_implication: Bidders must be aware that all submitted information, including pricing and other sensitive details, will become public record and cannot be kept confidential.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure that no sensitive or proprietary information is included in the bid packet unless explicitly requested; if necessary, seek clarification on how to protect confidential information.

quotes.quote: All bids submitted in response to Requests for Proposals (RFP’s) and Requests for Qualification (RFQ’s), documents contained within, and the details outlined on those documents become public record upon receipt by the City Clerk’s office and opening at the corresponding Board of Contract and Supply (BOCS) meeting.

findings.title: Disqualification for Direct Submission of Required Information
findings.fact: The City of Providence observes a public and transparent bidding process. Information required in the bidding packet may not be submitted directly to the issuing department at the discretion of the bidder in order to protect other information, such as pricing terms, from becoming public. Bidders who make such an attempt will be disqualified.
findings.business_implication: Bidders cannot attempt to bypass the public record by sending required information directly to the issuing department; doing so will result in disqualification.
findings.action_recommendation: Submit all required information in the bid packet as instructed; do not attempt to send required information separately to protect confidentiality.

quotes.quote: Information required in the bidding packet may not be submitted directly to the issuing department at the discretion of the bidder in order to protect other information, such as pricing terms, from becoming public. Bidders who make such an attempt will be disqualified.

findings.title: No Obligation to Redact Unrequested Sensitive Information
findings.fact: If sensitive information that has not been requested is enclosed or if a bidder opts to enclose the defined supplemental information prior to the issuing department’s request in the bidding packet submitted to the City Clerk, the City of Providence has no obligation to redact those details and bears no liability associated with the information becoming public record.
findings.business_implication: Bidders assume the risk of disclosing sensitive information if they include it voluntarily; the City will not redact it.
findings.action_recommendation: Do not include any sensitive or personal information unless explicitly requested; if such information is necessary, seek guidance on how to protect it.

quotes.quote: If sensitive information that has not been requested is enclosed or if a bidder opts to enclose the defined supplemental information prior to the issuing department’s request in the bidding packet submitted to the City Clerk, the City of Providence has no obligation to redact those details and bears no liability associated with the information becoming public record.

findings.title: Campaign Contribution Disclosure Requirement
findings.fact: Within the 12 month period preceding the date of this bid submission with the City of Providence, or with respect to the contracts that are not in writing within the 12 month period preceding the date of notification that the contract has reached the $100,000 threshold, have you made campaign contributions within a calendar year to (please list all persons or entities required under Sec. 21.-28.1 (e)).
findings.business_implication: Bidders must disclose any campaign contributions made to specified city officials and candidates within the past 12 months; failure to do so may affect eligibility.
findings.action_recommendation: Review campaign contribution records for the past 12 months and complete the affidavit accurately; ensure all required disclosures are made.

quotes.quote: Within the 12 month period preceding the date of this bid submission with the City of Providence, or with respect to the contracts that are not in writing within the 12 month period preceding the date of notification that the contract has reached the $100,000 threshold, have you made campaign contributions within a calendar year to (please list all persons or entities required under Sec. 21.-28.1 (e)).

findings.title: Affidavit of City Vendor Required
findings.fact: Per our Code of Ordinances Sec. 21.-28.1 (e), this form applies to a) the business, b) any political action committee whose name includes the name of the business, c) all persons holding ten (10) percent or greater equity interest or five thousand dollars ($5,000.00) or greater cash value interest in the business at any time during the reporting period, d) all executive officers of the business entity, e) any spouse or dependent child of any individual identified in a) though d) above.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must complete and sign the Affidavit of City Vendor, disclosing campaign contributions as required; this is a mandatory eligibility requirement.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure the affidavit is completed accurately and signed under the pains and penalties of perjury; gather necessary information about all covered individuals.

quotes.quote: Per our Code of Ordinances Sec. 21.-28.1 (e), this form applies to a) the business, b) any political action committee whose name includes the name of the business, c) all persons holding ten (10) percent or greater equity interest or five thousand dollars ($5,000.00) or greater cash value interest in the business at any time during the reporting period, d) all executive officers of the business entity, e) any spouse or dependent child of any individual identified in a) though d) above.

findings.title: Exemption for Non-Resident Executive Officers
findings.fact: Executive officers who are not residents of the state of Rhode Island are exempted from this requirement.
findings.business_implication: Non-resident executive officers are not required to report campaign contributions, but the bidder must still comply with other disclosure requirements.
findings.action_recommendation: Identify which executive officers are non-residents and ensure they are not incorrectly included in the disclosure; document the exemption.

quotes.quote: Executive officers who are not residents of the state of Rhode Island are exempted from this requirement.

findings.title: MBE/WBE Certification Required at Time of Bid
findings.fact: All MBE/WBE subcontractors/suppliers must be certified by the Office of Diversity, Equity and Opportunity at the time of bid.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must ensure that any MBE/WBE subcontractors/suppliers are certified before bid submission, or they cannot count toward the participation goal.
findings.action_recommendation: Verify the certification status of all intended MBE/WBE partners and obtain necessary documentation before bid submission.

quotes.quote: Please note that all MBE/WBE subcontractors/suppliers must be certified by the Office of Diversity, Equity and Opportunity at the time of bid.

findings.title: 20% MBE/WBE Participation Goal
findings.fact: The form indicates a 20% MBE/WBE combined participation goal, with a waiver request form if not met.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must either meet the 20% goal or submit a waiver request, which may affect bid competitiveness.
findings.action_recommendation: Assess ability to meet the goal and prepare waiver documentation if necessary.

quotes.quote: *If you did not meet the 20% MBE/WBE combined participation goal, submit a Waiver Request Form.

findings.title: Apprentice Requirements for Construction Projects
findings.fact: Construction projects valued at $100,000 or more must utilize not less than 15% of total hours worked by apprentices, and compliance reporting is a condition for payment.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must plan to meet apprentice hour requirements and submit compliance reports with payment requisitions, or risk delayed payments.
findings.action_recommendation: Incorporate apprentice utilization into project planning and establish reporting processes.

quotes.quote: This ordinance outlines requirements for utilizing not less than 15% of total hours worked by apprentices.
Compliance reporting shall be submitted with any contract payment requisition, in a format to be specified by the City.

findings.title: Post-Award Documentation Requirements
findings.fact: After award, the bidder must provide Business Tax ID, Proof of Insurance, and Certificate of Good Standing with the Rhode Island Secretary of State.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must be prepared to provide these documents promptly after award to avoid disqualification.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure these documents are readily available and current.

quotes.quote: You must be able to provide: • Business Tax ID will be requested after an award is approved by the Board of Contract and Supply. • Proof of Insurance. • Certificate of Good Standing with the Rhode Island Secretary of State.

findings.title: 60-Day Payment Terms
findings.fact: Invoices are payable sixty (60) days from receipt by the City, and no interest will be paid on overdue invoices.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must manage cash flow given the 60-day payment cycle and lack of interest on late payments.
findings.action_recommendation: Plan financial resources accordingly and consider the impact on cash flow.

quotes.quote: Invoices submitted to the City shall be payable sixty (60) days from the time of receipt by the City.
In no circumstances shall the City be obligated to pay or shall you be entitled to receive interest on any overdue invoice or payment.

findings.title: Broad Indemnification Obligation
findings.fact: The contractor must indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the City from any claims arising out of the work, including attorneys' fees.
findings.business_implication: The bidder assumes significant liability for claims, including legal costs, which could be substantial.
findings.action_recommendation: Review insurance coverage to ensure it adequately covers indemnification obligations.

quotes.quote: To the fullest extent permitted by law, you shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the City, its employees, officers, agents, and assigns from and against any and all claims, damages, losses, allegations, demands, actions, causes of action, suits, obligations, fines, penalties, judgments, liabilities, costs and expenses, including but not limited to attorneys’ fees, of any nature whatsoever arising out of, in connection with, or resulting from the performance of the work provided in the Agreement.

findings.title: Data Breach Notification Within 24 Hours
findings.fact: In the event of a breach of confidential/personal information, the contractor must notify the City within 24 hours of discovery.
findings.business_implication: The contractor must have robust incident response procedures to meet the tight notification deadline.
findings.action_recommendation: Implement a data breach response plan that ensures immediate notification to the City.

quotes.quote: In the event of a breach of such information, you shall notify the City of such breach immediately, but in no event later than twenty-four (24) hours after discovery of such breach.

findings.title: Mandatory Post-Award Meetings
findings.fact: After award, mandatory meetings will be scheduled to review apprenticeship and First Source requirements.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must allocate time and resources to attend these meetings and agree on compliance procedures.
findings.action_recommendation: Plan to attend mandatory meetings and prepare necessary documentation.

quotes.quote: Upon the contract being awarded to the successful bidder, a mandatory meeting will be scheduled to review the project requirements relative to apprenticeship requirements
Upon the contract being awarded to the successful bidder, a mandatory meeting will be scheduled to review the project requirements relative to the First Source Agreements

findings.title: 60-Day Payment Terms with No Interest
findings.fact: Invoices are payable sixty days from receipt, and the City is not obligated to pay interest on overdue invoices or any collection costs.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must finance operations for at least 60 days, and late payments will not accrue interest, impacting cash flow and profitability.
findings.action_recommendation: Factor 60-day payment terms into pricing and cash flow projections; consider requesting shorter payment terms or early payment discounts.

quotes.quote: Invoices submitted to the City shall be payable sixty (60) days from the time of receipt by the City.
In no circumstances shall the City be obligated to pay or shall you be entitled to receive interest on any overdue invoice or payment.

findings.title: Mandatory Apprentice and First Source Hiring Requirements
findings.fact: For construction projects valued at $100,000 or more, the Contractor must use at least 15% apprentice hours and comply with First Source hiring requirements for Providence residents, with compliance reporting as a condition for payment.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must recruit and train apprentices and hire Providence residents, which may increase labor costs and administrative burden; failure to comply may delay payments.
findings.action_recommendation: Assess ability to meet these requirements and include compliance costs in the bid; prepare to attend mandatory meetings and submit required reports.

quotes.quote: This ordinance outlines requirements for utilizing not less than 15% of total hours worked by apprentices.
This ordinance outlines requirements for hiring Providence residents to work on this project.
Compliance reporting shall be submitted with any contract payment requisition, in a format to be specified by the City.

findings.title: Financial Assurance Requirements
findings.fact: The bid form indicates that financial assurances may be required, and if the first two checkboxes are checked, the specified assurance must accompany the bid or the bid will not be considered. The third checkbox requires the lowest responsible bidder to post a bond.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must determine which financial assurance applies and provide the required bid bond or certified check with the bid, or risk disqualification.
findings.action_recommendation: Review the bid form to identify which checkboxes are marked and prepare the necessary financial assurance documents.

quotes.quote: If either of the first two checkboxes below is checked, the specified assurance must accompany a bid, or the bid will not be considered by the Board of Contract and Supply.
The third checkbox indicates the lowest responsible bidder will be contacted and required to post a bond to be awarded the contract.

findings.title: Public Record and Disqualification for Direct Submission
findings.fact: All bids become public record upon receipt, and bidders who attempt to submit sensitive information directly to the issuing department to protect pricing will be disqualified.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must be aware that all submitted information, including pricing, will be public; any attempt to circumvent this may lead to disqualification.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure all required information is included in the bid packet and avoid submitting sensitive information separately.

quotes.quote: All bids submitted in response to Requests for Proposals (RFP’s) and Requests for Qualification (RFQ’s), documents contained within, and the details outlined on those documents become public record upon receipt by the City Clerk’s office and opening at the corresponding Board of Contract and Supply (BOCS) meeting.
Bidders who make such an attempt will be disqualified.
